newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark's government to undergo January reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's government to undergo January reshuffle.

text.p: Denmark's Centre Democrats said on Friday they would leave the coalition government "as soon as is convenient" and Prime Minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen said the change would take effect in January.

A statement by the party said it was leaving because it was unhappy at the minority government's increasing dependence on the far left for its survival, but would continue to support the beleaguered government from outside the coalition.
"It is with regret that I have received the Centre Democrats' decision to leave the government," Rasmussen said.

"The Centre Democrats remain among the government's parliamentary supporters...the government will continue its work as before. The necessary changes to the composition of the government will take place in January," he said in a statement.
The coalition on Thursday won parliamentary approval for its 1997 budget ater forging a deal with the far left Socialist People's Party (SPP) and Unity List parties.

The Centre Democrats, who described themselves as the government's bulwark against the left, had publicly expressed disquiet about the alliance but said they waited until after the budget vote to announce their departure.
